source.title_on_document: One Does Not Simply Meme Alone: Evaluating Co-Creativity Between LLMs and Humans in the Generation of Humor

supplement.where: "supplementary material" (p. 5, Section 3.3; p. 6, Section 3.3); no URL given
supplement.holds: The full system prompts and the full list of AI-generated captions. The text does not say the supplement holds any statistics; all reported statistics are in the main text, Figures 6-8 and Table 1.

paper_design_summary: Prolific participants (124 recruited, 26 excluded for not completing) wrote meme captions for three image-topic combinations, either without help (human only) or with a GPT-4o chat interface during the ideation step (human-AI collaboration); a third condition had GPT-4o generate captions alone. 150 sampled memes per condition were then rated by a second set of Prolific participants (98 of 100 completed) on how funny, creative, and shareable they were. The paper also compares the number of ideas generated per participant between the two human conditions.

studies.label: Meme creation: human only vs human-AI collaboration (GPT-4o chat during ideation)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Condition: create meme captions without any assistance (baseline) or with access to a GPT-4o conversational interface during ideation. The paper calls it a between-subject study but does not say how participants were allocated to conditions. The only randomization it describes is of the image-topic permutation each participant received.
assignment.quote: we conducted a between-subject user study with three experimental groups.
assignment.locator: p. 4, Section 3; task randomization: p. 4, Section 3.2 ("The permutation of image and topic was selected randomly") and p. 6, Section 3.4

arms.name: Human only (baseline)
arms.description: Participants generated caption ideas and created memes "without external assistance by an AI tool or otherwise" (p. 4, Section 3.1).

arms.name: Human-AI collaboration
arms.description: Same task, with a chat interface to GPT-4o during the ideation step; favorite selection and image creation had no AI (p. 4, Section 3.1; p. 9, Section 5.1).

participants.exclusions: 124 recruited on Prolific; 26 excluded for not completing the task (p. 6, Section 3.6). The paper does not print 98 for this phase; 98 is 124 minus 26, and it matches 882 favorite ideas = 98 x 3 images x 3 favorites (p. 4, Section 3.2) and the 63 male + 35 female count (p. 6). Per-arm counts are not reported. The abstract says "three groups of 50 participants each" (p. 1), which conflicts with these counts. For the meme ratings, technical problems left 415 of the baseline favorites usable vs all 441 collaborative ones; one image template was then dropped, leaving 335 baseline and 307 collaborative memes, from which 150 per condition were sampled (pp. 4-5, Section 3.2).
participants.who: Prolific workers with good English skills who had used an LLM interface at least once; 30 countries; 63 male, 35 female; mean age 28.8 (sd 8.7). Separately, memes were rated by a second Prolific sample: N=100 recruited, 98 completed (rating at least 50 images), mean age 32.6 (sd 11.1), 29 countries.
participants.country: Multiple (30 countries for creators; 29 for raters)
participants.quote: we recruited 124 participants using the online platform Prolific. 26 participants were excluded due to not completing the task.

ai_tool.name_model: GPT-4o via the OpenAI API (p. 6, Section 3.4)
ai_tool.how_used: During the 4-5 minute ideation step per image, participants could enter any prompt into a chat interface. A system prompt framed it as a meme-idea helper and limited it to at most three ideas per response; the current image was sent to the LLM first. Ideas in LLM responses were automatically extracted and added to the participant's idea list. Participants then picked three favorites and placed them on the image without AI (pp. 4-5, Sections 3.1 and 3.3).

task.description: Write captions for meme templates (baby, boromir, doge, futurama, toy-story; a sixth, 'choice', was excluded) on one of three topics (work, food, sports). Each participant did three image-topic combinations: ideation, choose three favorites, add captions to the image.
task.duration: At least four and at most five minutes of ideation per image; whole session scheduled for no more than 40 minutes; 15 USD pay (p. 4, Section 3.2).

outcomes.name: Creative rating of memes
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Second Prolific sample (98 raters) each shown a random sample of 50 memes and asked how creative they considered them; the scale is not described in the text (Figure 8 axis runs 0-60+). Analyzed with three-group ANOVA and Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise t-tests. Per-topic ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis variants in Table 1 (work, sports, food). The paper does not say whether observations are individual ratings or meme-level averages.

contrasts.reported: No pairwise significance bracket between Human only and Human-AI in Figure 8; text: "Memes created by humans with the help of the LLM were not rated significantly different than those from the baseline, i.e. without AI, for any of the three dimensions." Omnibus three-group ANOVA (incl. AI only): Creative df 2, F 5.793, p 0.003 (Table 1, all topics).
contrasts.locator: p. 7, Figure 8 and Section 4.2; p. 8, Table 1

outcomes.name: Funny rating of memes
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Humor quality: raters judged how funny each meme was (same raters and procedure as S1-O1). ANOVA plus Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise t-tests; per-topic variants in Table 1.

contrasts.reported: No significance bracket between Human only and Human-AI in Figure 8; text states no significant difference for any of the three dimensions. Omnibus three-group ANOVA (incl. AI only): Funny df 2, F 6.971, p 0.001 (Table 1, all topics).
contrasts.locator: p. 7, Figure 8 and Section 4.2; p. 8, Table 1

outcomes.name: Shareable rating of memes
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Raters judged how likely they would be to share each meme. Kruskal-Wallis plus Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise Mann-Whitney-U tests (non-normal). Per-topic variants in Table 1.

contrasts.reported: No significance bracket between Human only and Human-AI in Figure 8; text states no significant difference for any of the three dimensions. Omnibus Kruskal-Wallis (incl. AI only): Shareable df 2, chi2 11.761, p 0.003 (Table 1, all topics).
contrasts.locator: p. 7, Figure 8 and Section 4.2; p. 8, Table 1

outcomes.name: Number of ideas generated
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Count of caption ideas in the participant's idea list during ideation. In the AI arm, ideas contained in LLM responses were automatically extracted and added to the list, so the count includes LLM-supplied ideas. Two variants: absolute number of ideas and average number of ideas per participant. Arm means are not reported; overall mean 6.1 (sd 3.2).

contrasts.reported: Shapiro-Wilk absolute W = 0.811, p < 0.001; average per participant W = 0.820, p < 0.001. Mann-Whitney-U: absolute count W = 12652, p < 0.001; average number of ideas 1519.5, p < 0.001. Figure 6 boxplot marked ***.

studies.label: AI-only memes vs human and human-AI memes (crowd ratings)

assignment.what_was_assigned: No person was assigned to AI. GPT-4o generated captions alone for each image-topic combination; these memes were rated alongside the S1 memes by the same rater sample. Raters each saw a random sample of 50 memes.
assignment.quote: In the third group, ideas were generated fully autonomously by the LLM.
assignment.locator: p. 4, Section 3.1; p. 5, Section 3.2; p. 6, Section 3.3

arms.name: AI only
arms.description: GPT-4o prompted to "generate 20 meme captions for this <image> about the topic of <topic>" for each of the 15 image-topic combinations; 150 memes rated (Figure 5 shows 300 AI meme images randomly sampled to 150; text says "giving us additional 150 images").

arms.name: Human only
arms.description: 150 sampled memes from S1 baseline participants.

arms.name: Human-AI collaboration
arms.description: 150 sampled memes from S1 AI-assisted participants.

participants.exclusions: Outputs, not people, are compared. Raters: N=100 recruited, 98 completed (p. 6, Section 3.6).
participants.who: AI output from GPT-4o; human outputs from S1 Prolific creators; ratings from 98 Prolific raters.
participants.quote: we simiarly recruited a second set of N=100 participants with the same prerequisites for language skills but knowledge of LLMs was not a requirement. 98 of these completed the task

ai_tool.how_used: Autonomous caption generation; image sent first, then the prompt asking for 20 captions per image-topic combination (p. 6, Section 3.3).

task.description: Meme captions for five templates on three topics (work, food, sports).
task.duration: Rating survey estimated at 10-15 minutes; 10 USD pay (p. 5, Section 3.2).

outcomes.name: Creative rating: AI only vs human-involved memes
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Same rating procedure as S1-O1; ANOVA and Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise t-tests. Per-topic variants in Table 1: work KW chi2 11.22 p 0.004; sports F 2.095 p 0.127; food F 0.608 p 0.546.

contrasts.reported: Figure 8 bracket Human only vs AI only: * (p < 0.05, Bonferroni-adjusted). Omnibus ANOVA all topics: df 2, F 5.793, p 0.003.
Figure 8 bracket Human-AI vs AI only: ** (p < 0.01, Bonferroni-adjusted).

outcomes.name: Funny rating: AI only vs human-involved memes
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Humor rating; ANOVA and pairwise t-tests, Bonferroni-adjusted. Per-topic variants in Table 1: work F 7.1 p 0.001; sports F 2.036 p 0.134; food KW chi2 3.455 p 0.177.

contrasts.reported: Figure 8 bracket Human only vs AI only: ** (p < 0.01). Omnibus ANOVA all topics: df 2, F 6.971, p 0.001.
Figure 8 bracket Human-AI vs AI only: * (p < 0.05).

outcomes.name: Shareable rating: AI only vs human-involved memes
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Shareability rating; Kruskal-Wallis and pairwise Mann-Whitney-U, Bonferroni-adjusted. Per-topic variants in Table 1: work KW chi2 8.470 p 0.014; sports F 1.712 p 0.184; food KW chi2 4.701 p 0.095.

contrasts.reported: Figure 8 bracket Human only vs AI only: * (p < 0.05). Omnibus Kruskal-Wallis all topics: df 2, chi2 11.761, p 0.003.
No bracket in Figure 8; text: "The only exception to this was 'shareability' where the comparison between the cooperative and pure AI creation was not significant."

company_involvement.description: No company authors or funders stated; GPT-4o accessed through the OpenAI API. Funding: HumanE-AI-Net, Grant Agreement ID 952026 (p. 10, Acknowledgments).

eligibility.reason: S1 compares people who worked with and without GPT-4o in a between-subject online study, but the paper never says how people were allocated to conditions; the only randomization described is of image-topic permutations (p. 4, Sections 3 and 3.2). If allocation was random it would be an online_rct with ai_vs_bau contrasts; otherwise quasi_people. Creator count: 124 recruited minus 26 non-completers = 98 across both human arms (not printed as one number; consistent with 882 favorites and 63+35 gender split, pp. 4 and 6); per-arm counts are not given and the abstract's "three groups of 50" conflicts. Outcomes are crowd ratings of the memes and idea counts. S2 (AI-only memes vs human memes) is ai_vs_human context.

one_line_finding: Participants with a GPT-4o chat generated more caption ideas than unassisted participants (Mann-Whitney W = 12652, p < 0.001; p. 6, Fig. 6), but their memes were not rated differently on funny, creative, or shareable, while AI-only memes were rated higher than both human conditions (omnibus F = 6.971, 5.793, chi2 = 11.761; p. 7 Fig. 8, p. 8 Table 1).
open_questions: Were participants randomly assigned to the human-only and human-AI conditions? The paper does not say.
How many participants were in each human arm? Only the total (124 recruited, 26 excluded) is given; the abstract says groups of 50.
Are the rating analyses run on individual ratings or on meme-level means? The rating scale is also not described.
Pairwise statistics and arm means/SDs for the Human-AI vs Human-only rating contrasts are not printed (figure only).
notes: Self-report outcomes not listed as outcomes: NASA-TLX raw workload (t = -0.955, df = 88.811, p = 0.342) and Effort subscale (Mann-Whitney W = 755, p = 0.027, lower with LLM); perceived number of ideas (W = 1308.5, p = 0.043); perceived ownership (W = 562, p < 0.001, higher without LLM) (pp. 6-7, Sections 4.1.2-4.1.3, Figure 7). Figure 1 shows top-4 memes per metric (descriptive only). Figure 8 caption labels both p < 0.01 and p < 0.001 as '**' (typo). Text gives shareability Shapiro-Wilk p < 0.001 while Table 1 prints 0.001. The AI arm's idea count includes ideas extracted automatically from LLM responses. Figure 6 boxplot and Figure 8 violin plots carry the only arm-level distributions; no arm means are printed.
